SMTO-MEM-0032 — Smart memory matching is off for your current model

GUID: ce0d0894-df79-5a25-9584-88465f669b9c
Slug: knowledge-memory-relevance-calibration-required
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • SMTO is set to hide weak memory matches, but it only knows the right cut-off for its standard matching model. With the model you chose, it skipped matching by meaning and used keyword matching instead.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Agent behavior › Knowledge. Under Search and ranking, turn off Filter weak semantic matches. With the filter off, SMTO no longer needs a cut-off for your model and can match memories by meaning again.
  2. If you want to keep the filter, ask the person who manages SMTO to set Optional semantic score threshold under Advanced settings › Memory retrieval on the same page, for the model you use. The filter needs a cut-off tested for your model; the built-in one only fits SMTO's default model.
  3. Open Knowledge, go to Semantic memory, type a question and select Preview selected memories. This shows whether meaning-based matching works again.

What success looks like

  • The memory preview returns results without this warning.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting which text embedding model is selected in Knowledge settings. Your saved memories are not changed by this; keyword matching keeps working meanwhile.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Backend.search refused semantic Memory search because memory_relevance_filter is on, no score_threshold is set, and the selected embedding model is not the calibrated local BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 (768) encoder.

What this means

  • The selected encoder cannot yet apply the configured Memory relevance filtering. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported memory_relevance_calibration_required. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • Semantic retrieval accepts the configured encoder.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • In Settings › Agent behavior › Knowledge, either turn off “Filter weak semantic matches”, or set “Optional semantic score threshold” under Advanced settings › Memory retrieval to a value validated for the selected encoder, or switch the Memory embedding back to local BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 (768 dimensions), whose calibrated threshold is 0.55. Thresholds must not be copied between models.
  • Ask an administrator to review the selected embedding encoder in model settings. Use the supported encoder configuration before retrying semantic Memory retrieval.

Retry and execution caution

  • Semantic retrieval accepts the configured encoder.

How to verify the fix

  • Semantic retrieval accepts the configured encoder.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.
